mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the past month signals monetary easing, which reduces borrowing costs and increases consumer and business spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS declines but SPX posts negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases, or if the Rank IC falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% indicates a strong labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by >0.2pp in one month
failure_condition: If UNRATE drops below 5% but SPX returns are negative in more than 35% of cases, or if the signal's IC is not significantly positive.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals strong economic activity, which boosts corporate revenues and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO grows by >1% MoM but SPX returns are negative in more than 30% of cases, or if the signal's IC is not significantly positive.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% month-over-month indicates increased demand in the housing market, which spills over into broader economic activity and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST rises by >5% MoM but SPX returns are negative in more than 35% of cases, or if the signal's IC is not significantly positive.

mechanism_narrative: When both consumer spending (RSAFS) and employment (PAYEMS) increase simultaneously, it signals strong aggregate demand, which drives corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If both RSAFS and PAYEMS increase but SPX returns are negative in more than 35% of cases, or if the signal's IC is not significantly positive.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% during a monetary tightening cycle increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises above 4.5% but SPX returns are positive in more than 40% of cases, or if the signal's IC is not significantly negative.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) at an annualized rate of >3% signals strong economic growth, which drives corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 grows at >3% annualized rate but SPX returns are negative in more than 30% of cases, or if the signal's IC is not significantly positive.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% month-over-month signals rising inflationary pressures, which may lead to monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL rises by >0.5% MoM but SPX returns are positive in more than 35% of cases, or if the signal's IC is not significantly negative.
